doc.purpose: Dolphin profile tree content as data: every INI body lives here, substituted by the generic profile compiler. Each player is a row (for_each players: its pad, its seat and its layout); controller_layouts give each Wii layout its extension, Wii Remote source and how it switches, and each live layout of each connected player gets its own profile file under Config/Semu Layouts, which the supervisor hands Dolphin through its profile cycle (emulator.json controllers).
doc.grammar: Dolphin's control-expression wire format: backtick controls, `<device>:<control>` qualified references, @(...) hotkey chords whose key names are XInput2's (chord_encoding.keys: Return, BackSpace, space, KP_Add, minus), (`KEY` & !`Ctrl`) for a keyboard alternate no Semu chord may press.
doc.aspect: GFX.ini pins AspectRatio = 5 (AspectMode::CustomStretch) at 4:3, the gc and wii display.aspect, so Dolphin draws exactly the SEMU_RENDER_ASPECT rectangle the compositor cuts (1067x800 on the Deck). Auto, the default, and Force 4:3 both draw at the VI's analog aspect (about 1.26 on GameCube), which left Dolphin's own black bars inside the cut. Both custom values are set because they default to 1:1.
doc.disc_change: Dolphin.ini [Core] AutoDiscChange = True: Dolphin loads a GameCube playlist itself but defaults MAIN_AUTO_DISC_CHANGE to false, so at the disc-change prompt the game would eject and wait for a file dialog Semu never shows. With it on, Dolphin inserts the next playlist entry when the game stops the motor or ejects. It acts only on a boot from an .m3u, so single discs and Wii titles are unaffected.
doc.save_states: Save and load bind Dolphin's Save to Selected Slot and Load from Selected Slot (HotkeyManager.cpp:143,155, groups :320-321), the slot Increase/Decrease Selected State Slot moves, so the slot Semu shows is the one Dolphin uses. Dolphin keeps the selected slot in Qt.ini [Emulation] StateSlot (DolphinQt/Settings.cpp:576-584); Semu writes that file with slot 1 each launch, which is where Semu's counter starts too (MainWindow.cpp:300-301, 1582-1596 wrap 1..10).
doc.speed: Dolphin 2606a (c77bbaa) ships desktop defaults that stutter on the Deck: single core (MainSettings.cpp:59-65, DEFAULT_CPU_THREAD true only on Android) and synchronous shader compiles (GraphicsSettings.cpp:110-111), so every new shader stalls a frame. Dolphin.ini [Core] CPUThread = True runs the GPU thread beside the CPU thread; a GameSettings INI that needs one core (98 say CPUThread = False) still wins, as GlobalGame is searched ahead of Base (Common/Config/Enums.h:39-47). GFX.ini ShaderCompilationMode = 2 is AsynchronousUberShaders, the UI's Hybrid Ubershaders (VideoConfig.h:43-49): an ubershader draws while the specialised shader compiles in the background, which OpenGL on radeonsi supports (OGLConfig.cpp:688-690). WaitForShadersBeforeStarting stays at Dolphin's False: with ubershaders on it would queue every ubershader pipeline and block the boot until all compiled (ShaderCache.cpp:69-75), a long black screen on the first boot after a release. visual.performance_overlay turns on ShowFPS, ShowSpeed and LogRenderTimeToFile, which writes one line per frame to Logs/render_times.txt and per VI to Logs/vblank_times.txt in the user directory (PerformanceMetrics.h:53-54, PerformanceTracker.cpp:187-198); Dolphin draws the overlay at the window's top-right (PerformanceMetrics.cpp:170-171), outside the 4:3 picture the compositor cuts on a 16:10 screen, so on the Deck the log is the measure.
doc.quit: General/Stop is bound only on macOS: on Linux the supervisor reads every keyboard and quits the process group itself, so Ctrl+Q is Semu's alone there.
doc.wiimote: The Wii Remote, Nunchuk and Classic Controller read their buttons, d-pad, sticks and triggers from the player's own SDL pad (${dolphin_pad}, the player row's identity), with Dolphin's SDL control names. Player 1 aims with the XInput2 pointer (wiimote_pointer_body: Device = ${dolphin_pointer}, every pad control qualified) and reads motion from ${dolphin_motion}, the Deck's own controller through Dolphin's SteamDeck backend, which opens hidraw (SteamDeck.cpp:143,175); players 2 to 4 aim with their right stick (wiimote_stick_body: Device = their pad, XInput-signed halves, Y+ up) and have no motion, so no profile of one player names another player's device. So the open Semu menu's EVIOCGRAB of the pads covers every Wii button, the Deck's grips (L4, R4, L5, R5), which Steam's template holds for its Hotkeys and Wii presets, reach no Wii control, and each name exists on the device it is read from (native_controls). The keyboard alternates on the XInput2 pointer device are written (`KEY` & !`Ctrl`): every Semu chord holds Ctrl, so a chord Steam types never also presses a Wii button. Keys are backticked: Dolphin lexes a bare digit as a number (ExpressionParser.cpp:172-181, 252-253), so the old Buttons/1 = 1|... and Buttons/2 = 2|... held 1 and 2 down for good.
doc.pointer: The Wii Remote IR reads the X pointer the right trackpad moves (IR/Up/Down/Left/Right = `Cursor Y-/Y+/X-/X+` on ${pointer}), and libsemupreload hands Dolphin that pointer on the bezelled picture as the point Dolphin drew there (wii surface_mapping.pointer_screen), so the IR follows the finger. The IR keeps Dolphin's own defaults, chosen to reach the screen edges in most games (Cursor.cpp:34-62): Vertical Offset 10, Total Yaw 25, Total Pitch 20, Auto-Hide off; with Auto-Hide on the pointer vanished 2.5 s after it last moved and no button brought it back (Cursor.cpp:139-163). Dolphin.ini [Interface] CursorVisibility = 0 (ShowCursor::Never, MainSettings.h:255-260) blanks the X arrow over the render window, so the one pointer seen is the game's own; Semu draws no arrow on Wii (its cursor is for touch screens only).
doc.layouts: Layouts switch through Dolphin's own profile cycle: Hotkeys.ini binds Controller Profile N/Next Profile (HotkeyScheduler.cpp:303-321) to the layout_hotkeys chords, and a press loads the next file of Config/Profiles/Wiimote (DoFileSearch, sorted, recursive, FileSearch.cpp) into Wii Remote N with its Device line (UpdateToProfile, InputProfile.cpp:76-90), keeping one index for all four remotes (m_wiimote_profile_index). The GameCube layout disconnects the Wii Remote (WiimoteSource 0) and plays on the GameCube pad (SIDevice 6), which Dolphin reads at boot, so it applies by restarting the game. The Undo Load/Save State hotkeys are not bound: Dolphin matches superset modifiers, so a bare F12 fired on Steam's Ctrl+Shift+F12.
doc.osd: OnScreenDisplayMessages = False keeps every Dolphin OSD message (MAIN_OSD_MESSAGES, OnScreenDisplay.cpp:157 at c77bbaa0) off the composed picture, as PCSX2's OsdMessagesPos = 0 does: Internal Resolution: 2x at a live Render Scale, a controller profile loaded at a live layout switch, a state saved. Semu's own toasts announce each of them.

native_shortcuts.why: Once Hotkeys.ini has a section, InputConfig::LoadConfig loads it and ControlGroup::LoadConfig reads every control the file leaves out as an empty expression; HotkeyManager::LoadDefaults (HotkeyManager.cpp:395-476) runs only without the file. Semu writes the whole [Hotkeys] section, so none of the defaults apply, among them Skylanders Portal on Ctrl+P, which would fire beside Toggle Pause.
native_shortcuts.superset_source: dolphin c77bbaa Source/Core/InputCommon/ControlReference/ExpressionParser.cpp:565-590: a hotkey expression fires when its key and modifiers are held, extra modifiers included ("This also allows superset modifiers to function"), so Ctrl+A also fires on Ctrl+Shift+A

native_controls.source: dolphin 2606a Source/Core/InputCommon/ControllerInterface: SDL/SDLGamepad.h:17-30 (legacy Button N, Axis N+/-, Hat N NESW) and 383-427 (gamepad buttons, axes as XInput-signed halves, motion axes), SDL/SDLGamepad.cpp:93-103,131-136,220-221,472 (outputs and sensors); SteamDeck/SteamDeck.cpp:196-264; Xlib/XInput2.cpp:234-244 (combined modifiers), 441-461 (keys: XKeysymToString of the unshifted keysym, letters upper-cased), 482-493 (Click N, Cursor X/Y +/-)
native_controls.patterns: Besides the lists: SDL also names Axis <n>+/-, Button <n> and Hat <n> N/E/S/W (its legacy joystick inputs); XInput2 names Click <n>, F1 to F24, and every letter and digit as its upper-case keysym.
